headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad API egress can leak or act on Pathway-derived outputs, while Pathway itself adds little isolation and no direct mitigation is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no clipboard, browser, MCP, shell, or filesystem write surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest RD-Agent output by default. RD-Agent can run browsers and call APIs, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel, making prompt injection mainly a manual or external-bridge risk.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies RD-Agent output into Pathway inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and prompts.
Add a provenance label to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: introduce a trusted-content filter before Pathway ingests external text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway touches no data classes and has no network egress, but RD-Agent handles financial reports, logs, execution traces, and API secrets while also calling external APIs. If Pathway outputs are fed into RD-Agent, sensitive content can leave the local boundary through RD-Agent’s default egress.
conditions: IF Pathway outputs contain sensitive documents and are passed into RD-Agent, leakage is possible.
IF RD-Agent is configured with its documented API keys, those inputs can be transmitted to third-party services.
mitigations: Do not route sensitive Pathway outputs into RD-Agent.
Redact secrets before any transfer.
Use a separate non-production API key for testing.
Review RD-Agent logs for sensitive fields.
requires-engineering: add an egress allowlist and content classifier.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Pathway cannot write files, modify git, or use the network, so it has no meaningful write conflict surface. RD-Agent can use multiple instances and writes logs, but without Pathway write access or shared mutable state, overlap is limited and not dangerous by default.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is introduced, concurrent log or artifact writes may conflict.
IF Pathway is wrapped with additional write permissions, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Keep Pathway read-only.
Separate log directories per agent.
Avoid shared git working trees.
Use per-agent output folders.
requires-engineering: add file locking for any shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: RD-Agent is an automation/research agent with browser and API access, so if it consumes Pathway-produced outputs as authoritative, it may propagate errors into downstream actions. Pathway is a document-processing system, so its outputs can be treated as facts unless explicitly verified.
conditions: IF RD-Agent uses Pathway outputs without a verification step, incorrect facts can cascade.
IF RD-Agent is allowed to act on those outputs in browser/API workflows, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before downstream actions.
Add a verification step for Pathway-derived facts.
Tag Pathway outputs as untrusted by default.
Limit RD-Agent to read-only analysis mode.
requires-engineering: implement citation and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: RD-Agent explicitly handles financial reports, logs, execution traces, and API secrets, while Pathway’s profile shows no data classes or residency controls. Because RD-Agent also uses third-party APIs, compliance gaps are plausible when regulated or secret-bearing data flows from Pathway into RD-Agent; Pathway is not cited separately because it exposes no specific compliance controls.
conditions: IF regulated data from Pathway is processed by RD-Agent, residency or retention obligations may apply.
IF RD-Agent sends those materials to external APIs without a DPA, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Classify data before transfer.
Block regulated data from external API calls.
Confirm a DPA for any third-party model use.
Minimize log retention.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
